title: Tensoring a finitely presented module commutes with arbitrary products
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $P$ a finitely presented $R$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. For every set $A$ and every family $(Q_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}$ of $R$-modules, the canonical $R$-linear map $\theta_{P,(Q_\alpha)}:P\otimes_R\prod_{\alpha\in A}Q_\alpha\longrightarrow\prod_{\alpha\in A}(P\otimes_RQ_\alpha)$, given by $p\otimes(q_\alpha)_\alpha\mapsto(p\otimes q_\alpha)_\alpha$, is bijective. Tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and products consist of all families with componentwise module operations. The index set $A$ need not be finite, and no finiteness or flatness is assumed for the $Q_\alpha$.

proof.text: By [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], choose finite natural numbers m,n and an exact sequence of R-modules R^m \xrightarrow{d} R^n \xrightarrow{\pi} P \to 0. The same fixed presentation will be used for every family (Q_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}; the cases m=0, n=0 and A=\varnothing are allowed by the definition.

source.place: Tag 059K, proposition-fp-tensor, proof (1) implies (2), first sentence choosing R^m → R^n → M.

proof.text: Tensor the chosen presentation with the product module Q=\prod_{\alpha\in A}Q_\alpha and, separately, with each Q_\alpha. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], both resulting rows are right exact. For a finite free module R^r, the canonical map R^r\otimes_R Q\to\prod_\alpha(R^r\otimes_RQ_\alpha) is an isomorphism: using the standard basis, both sides identify with Q^r and the map is componentwise the identity. Under these identifications the two rows form a commutative diagram, because the tensor-induced map is determined on pure tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 059K, proposition-fp-tensor, proof (1) implies (2), displayed tensor diagram and the assertion that the first two vertical maps are isomorphisms.

proof.text: The bottom comparison map is surjective. Indeed, given a family in \prod_\alpha(P\otimes_RQ_\alpha), lift it along the bottom surjection from \prod_\alpha(R^n\otimes_RQ_\alpha), use the finite-free isomorphism of Step 2 to lift that element to R^n\otimes_RQ, and map it along the top row to P\otimes_RQ. Commutativity sends the resulting element to the original family.

source.place: Tag 059K, proposition-fp-tensor, proof (1) implies (2), diagram chase proving surjectivity.

proof.text: The bottom comparison map is injective. Let x\in P\otimes_RQ map to zero. Lift x to b\in R^n\otimes_RQ by top-row surjectivity. Its image b\prime in \prod_\alpha(R^n\otimes_RQ_\alpha) maps to zero in the bottom-right product, so bottom-row exactness gives a\prime in \prod_\alpha(R^m\otimes_RQ_\alpha) mapping to b\prime. The finite-free isomorphism in Step 2 lifts a\prime to a\in R^m\otimes_RQ. Since the left and middle vertical maps are isomorphisms, the image of a in R^n\otimes_RQ equals b; hence x=0. Therefore the comparison is bijective.

source.place: Tag 059K, proposition-fp-tensor, proof (1) implies (2), diagram chase proving injectivity.
